summary: Jean Deloche was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He taught at Suryavarman II School (1961–1962), directed the Alliance Française of Madras (1962–1966), and held research posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (from 1966) and the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1992–2019).

Indologist Jean Filliozat studied at the EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He was a professor at the EPHE (1941–1978) and Collège de France (1951–1978), and directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1956–1977) and the French Institute of Pondicherry (1955–1977).

Jean Kellens worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology, studying at the University of Liège (~1962–1966) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1968–1974). He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1974–1993), Liège (~1993–2000), and the Collège de France (1993).

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at the University of Amsterdam. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and Leiden University (1914–1939), also directing the Kern Institute.

Jean Przyluski worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss at the EPHE and ENFOM. He held professorships at INALCO (1923–1930), the EPHE (1926–1944), and the Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean Rouch studied at École des Ponts ParisTech, the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and the Institut d'ethnologie under Marcel Mauss (~1941–1942). He later held an academic post at Paris Nanterre University.

Jean-Baptiste Biot worked in history, archaeology, and Sinology after studying at Collège Louis-le-Grand, École des Ponts ParisTech, and École Polytechnique. He held professorships at the Collège de France (1800–1862) and the Science Faculty of Paris (1809–1862).

Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who was educated at Lycée Claude Fauriel, École du Louvre, and the University of Paris. He served as director (1986–2004) and president (~1986–2008) of the Musée Guimet.

Philosopher Jean-François Lyotard studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the University of Paris, and Paris Nanterre University. He held academic posts at the University of Paris (1959–1967), Paris Nanterre (1967–1970), Paris 8 (1972–1987), and the University of California, Irvine (~1987–1998).
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who studied at the Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, the Lycée du Parc (~1941–1943), and the École Normale Supérieure (1943).

Linguist Jean-Louis Burnouf studied at Lycée Saint-Louis and under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served as professor of rhetoric at Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1817) and held the chair of Latin eloquence at the Collège de France (1816–1844).
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and holds a post at the CNRS.

Jean-Luc Chevillard works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1975) and under Antoine Culioli (~1980–1989), later holding posts as a CNRS researcher (~1989) and a lecturer at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Jean-Noël Robert works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at INALCO and under Bernard Frank, later holding posts at CNRS (1975–1990), EPHE (from 1979), and as director at the Collège de France (2010–2022).

Sinologist and linguist Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat studied at INALCO under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as president of the conservatory at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1832).

Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Burgundy Europe, INALCO, and under Yves Hervouet, later serving as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1998–2004).

Jeannine Auboyer was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at the École du Louvre, EPHE, and University of Paris under scholars including Hackin, Grousset, and Stern. She served as chief curator at the Musée Guimet and taught at École du Louvre (1965–1980).

Jeff Dolven studied at Yale University and the University of Oxford. He was a junior fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows (~1996–1999) and became a professor of English at Princeton University (~1999).

Philosopher Jeff Malpas studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. He was head of philosophy at Murdoch University (~1989–1999) and served as a professor and later Emeritus Distinguished Professor (2018) at the University of Tasmania.

Jeff Ralph works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a degree in religious studies at Queen's University at Kingston and completed his thesis at the University of Victoria under doctoral supervisor Duncan M. Taylor.
